The published wasmtime 42.0.1 crate requires rustc >= 1.91.0 (edition 2024), newer than this repository's root rust-toolchain.toml (channel 1.88.0, pinned for producing wasm32-wasip1 artifacts); this is not a blocker because tests/compat/runtime/invoker is a standalone host-side test tool that produces no wasm32-wasip1 output and is never linked into StarlingMonkey itself. It carries its own nested tests/compat/runtime/invoker/rust-toolchain.toml pinning exact Rust 1.91.0 (profile=minimal, host-only), independently of and without changing the repository root's toolchain; rustup resolves the nearest rust-toolchain.toml by walking up from cwd, and both tests/compat/runtime/lib/run_bridge_tests.py's build_invoker() and tests/compat/reference/run-reference.mjs invoke cargo with an absolute cwd inside invoker/, so this is honored regardless of the caller's own working directory. See tests/compat/runtime/README.md's 'Wasmtime version' section for the exact API adaptations (invoker/src/main.rs) and verification commands.

verified_by_reference_run.description: Every fixture below except the two negative fixtures was actually componentized with the pinned npm package (@bytecodealliance/componentize-js@0.21.0, which required a portable Node.js >=22 since the environment's default Node 20.14 cannot load that package's native optional dependencies) and executed through Wasmtime -- specifically tests/compat/runtime/invoker's dynamic Component Model API on the official `wasmtime` Rust crate, without another component transpiler -- to record real observed reference values rather than assumed ones. The two negative fixtures were run through the same componentize() call to observe componentization-time behavior (no wasm execution involved for those two). This one-time verification pass is not part of normal CI; tests/compat/reference/ lets it be reproduced with one command (`npm install && node run-reference.mjs`).
verified_by_reference_run.environment_note: This repository does not depend on Node/npm normally; the verification pass above used a temporary, non-committed Node 22 install and is not required to build or test this repository. Direct Wasmtime execution ensures observed defects (see known_deviations componentizejs-u32-high-bit-defect) are attributable to ComponentizeJS itself, not to a second adapter.

bridge.description: Zig/WABT dispatch bridge (runtime/js_dispatch.cpp + runtime/js_dispatch.zig): a WABT-generated per-export Zig shell dispatches through one of two paths, chosen at bindgen time per export signature. Signatures containing only bool/numeric-scalar/string/list/record shapes that fit losslessly in JSON text still JSON-encode their arguments, call starling_js_dispatch(), which JSON.parses them into a JS array and applies it as positional arguments to a same-named (or camelCase-fallback-named) root export or member of the matching named-interface namespace object, then JSON.stringifies the return value back across the boundary. Any signature containing an option (at any depth), i64/u64 (anywhere, including nested), char, tuple, enum, flags, variant, result<T,E>, or list<u8> instead routes through a native tagged-value tree (runtime/js_dispatch.{h,cpp,zig}'s STARLING_JS_* tags), preserving exact BigInt precision, distinguishing `string` from `list<u8>` (both `[]const u8` under plain Zig reflection; disambiguated by a generated `wit_types.ByteList`/`wit_types.Char` wrapper type emitted by the WABT bindgen) and doing deep-copied, strictly-validated lifting/lowering with no JSON text involved. Wrong JavaScript kinds or invalid discriminants trap, while correct numeric kinds wrap with ComponentizeJS-compatible ECMAScript semantics. Promise/thenable results are pumped to settlement and then lowered normally. The same tagged-value tree drives reverse JavaScript calls to host-provided versioned-interface and root-function WIT imports through WABT `--js-imports` wrappers; this compatibility harness exercises the export direction, with dedicated import coverage in tests/e2e/wit-imports/.

known_deviations.summary: The pinned ComponentizeJS reference rejects a WIT-declared export that JavaScript does not implement (or implements as a non-function) at componentization time, with a message naming the missing/invalid export. The current Zig/WABT bridge resolves the JS export lazily by name on each call (see js_dispatch.cpp's JS_GetProperty/JS::IsCallable check), so the same mistake is only observed as a call-time trap, not a componentization-time failure: build-verified by actually building and componentizing both negative fixtures' reactors and invoking the missing/invalid export through Wasmtime (tests/compat/runtime), which traps rather than failing componentization. The wasm trap itself carries no message text (a bare `unreachable`); the descriptive "... is not a function" diagnostic is printed by the JS engine's own panic handler to the guest's stderr stream, which tests/compat/runtime/invoker captures alongside the trap for comparison.

Empirically, values of a plain `u32` argument/result at or above 2^31 (2147483648) did not round-trip correctly through the pinned ComponentizeJS 0.21.0 reference in this environment (e.g. echou32(4294967295) returned 4292870144, echou32(2147483648) returned 0), even in a minimal single-function isolated world. This was re-verified by invoking the real componentize-js output directly through Wasmtime (tests/compat/runtime/invoker), with no other transpiler in the call path, so the defect is attributable to ComponentizeJS/its embedded engine itself, not to a transpilation adapter. Root cause not diagnosed here (candidates include the embedded engine's own canonical-ABI numeric lifting/lowering); root-caused and either fixed upstream or worked around in a later phase. The current Zig/WABT bridge (runtime/js_dispatch.zig, which serializes numbers as JSON decimal text parsed by JS as an exact float64) has been build-verified unaffected: the actual reactor was built and its echou32 export invoked through Wasmtime for the same boundary values (0, 2147483647, 2147483648, 4294967295), all of which round-tripped correctly (see fixtures/numeric-primitives runtime_verification).
known_deviations.confidence: wasmtime-verified (defect, no transpiler adapter involved), build-verified (bridge unaffected)

known_deviations.summary: RESOLVED as of sync-value-parity for u64 and non-negative s64: any signature containing i64/u64 (scalar, nested in a record/option/list, or as a plain argument/result) routes through the native tagged-value bridge (runtime/js_dispatch.zig), which exchanges exact full-domain JS BigInt values with no JSON-text round-trip, matching the pinned ComponentizeJS reference's own BigInt lifting exactly for every value the reference itself can accept, including values >= 2^63 and wraparound arithmetic. known_deviations.summary: Empirically, the pinned ComponentizeJS 0.21.0 reference unconditionally traps (wasm `unreachable`, guest stderr diagnostic 'Redirecting call to abort() to mozalloc_abort') on *any* negative-valued `s64`, whether as an argument or as a return value, regardless of magnitude -- not just near the i64::MIN boundary: a minimal isolated probe world (`id-s64: func(v: s64) -> s64` returning its argument unchanged; `neg-s64: func(v: s64) -> s64` returning `-v`) shows `id-s64(-5)` and `neg-s64(5)` (i.e. returning -5) both trap, while `id-s64(0)`/`neg-s64(0)` and large positive s64 near i64::MAX succeed. u64 (which has no negative values), and negative s8/s16/s32 (exercised elsewhere by numeric-primitives/records/advanced-types' checked-negate), are unaffected -- this is specific to the `s64` lifting/lowering path. Re-verified directly through Wasmtime (tests/compat/runtime/invoker) against the real componentize-js output with no other transpiler in the call path, so the defect is attributable to ComponentizeJS/its embedded engine itself. A trap also poisons the shared Wasmtime component instance for every subsequent call in the same invocation (Wasmtime's own component-model reentrancy semantics), so this cannot be exercised as an ordinary passing case inside a shared-instance fixture batch like tests/compat/fixtures/integers-64bit's; see that fixture's own notes. The current Zig/WABT native bridge (runtime/js_dispatch.zig) is unaffected: build-verified via tests/e2e/native-dispatch/run.sh's 'big-sub near i64::MIN' case (a negative s64 argument and a negative s64 result, both exact).
known_deviations.confidence: wasmtime-verified (defect, no transpiler adapter involved), build-verified (bridge unaffected)
known_deviations.evidence: Reproduced against the pinned reference (tests/compat/reference's pinned @bytecodealliance/componentize-js@0.21.0, commit 12c2b4a25033f65047f8ec5c5fb9e3013bfc4950) via tests/compat/runtime/invoker (compat-invoker) using an isolated single-function probe world, not embedded in the checked-in fixture set because the resulting trap poisons the shared component instance for later calls; tests/e2e/native-dispatch/run.sh 'big-sub near i64::MIN' shows the bridge itself handling the same value class correctly.

known_deviations.summary: Not a behavioral deviation from the reference, but an internal architecture note: WIT `string` and `list<u8>` both reflect as the identical Zig type `[]const u8`, so the native bridge cannot distinguish them from runtime data alone (and must not guess). Resolved by generating a nominal wrapper type (`wit_types.ByteList`) at the WABT bindgen boundary for `list<u8>` specifically (leaving `string` as plain `[]const u8`), giving the native lifting/lowering code an unambiguous compile-time type to dispatch on; likewise `char` (which also reflects as plain `u32` in Zig) is wrapped as `wit_types.Char`. This is a code-generation-time distinction, never a runtime heuristic.
known_deviations.evidence: wabt worktree (feat/sync-value-parity-types, commit 5ee61e0787f95b43593111846eff9931746ab0ea): src/wit_types.zig, build/bindgen/component_bindgen.zig; runtime/js_dispatch.zig's encodeNative/decodeNative special-casing of wit_types.Char/wit_types.ByteList before the generic type switch

known_deviations.summary: A Promise/thenable returned from a synchronous WIT export's JS implementation is now pumped to completion: runtime/event_loop.{h,cpp}'s EventLoop::pump_until_promise_settled drives the existing job/microtask queue (js::RunJobs) and, for macrotask-driven promises (e.g. setTimeout), the existing async task queue (api::AsyncTask::select) -- reusing engine machinery rather than a busy spin or arbitrary sleep -- until the promise settles, then js_dispatch.cpp's resolve_promise_like feeds the fulfilled value into the normal typed/JSON result conversion, matching the pinned ComponentizeJS 0.21.0 reference's ability to synchronously drive a Promise-returning export to completion. Non-Promise thenables are duck-typed and normalized via JS::NewPromiseObject + JS::ResolvePromise (the engine's own PromiseResolve semantics), not a hand-rolled `.then()` call. A rejection is surfaced as a call-time trap carrying the rejection's message (Engine::dump_promise_rejection). If both queues are exhausted while the promise is still pending, pump_until_promise_settled returns PromisePumpResult::NoProgress and resolve_promise_like traps deterministically with an explicit diagnostic, rather than looping forever -- see fixtures/promises-deadlock. The pump function is keyed directly on the specific promise's JS::GetPromiseState, not on Engine::run_event_loop's shared interest counter (which timers.cpp's setTimeout does not increment and which can report 'complete' before a queued async task actually runs), so event-loop state is not shared or perturbed across unrelated dispatch calls and one call's rejection/no-progress outcome cannot poison a later call.
known_deviations.evidence: runtime/event_loop.h, runtime/event_loop.cpp, runtime/js_dispatch.cpp (resolve_promise_like); tests/e2e/native-dispatch/run.sh (promise-resolve-add, promise-add, promise-reject, thenable-add, promise-timeout-add, promise-notify, promise-resolve-point, promise-deadlock, and the BigInt/native-dispatch equivalents, all passing through the real Wasmtime 42 CLI bundled by this repository's build.zig.zon, 2026-07-14); tests/compat/fixtures/promises, tests/compat/fixtures/promises-rejected, tests/compat/fixtures/promises-deadlock (tests/compat/runtime/run-bridge-tests.sh, real Wasmtime 42 crate invoker, 2026-07-14)

known_deviations.summary: feat/js-bridge-parity-integration reconciliation (sync-value-parity's top-level result<T,E> exports x promise-sync's Promise pumping): before this integration, runtime/js_dispatch.cpp's resolve_promise_like treated *every* Promise rejection as an unconditional call-time trap, regardless of whether the export's own return type was a WIT result<T,E> -- correct for a non-result export, but never verified for a result-returning one. Re-checked directly against the pinned ComponentizeJS 0.21.0 reference (not assumed): a rejected Promise on a top-level result<T,E> export is indistinguishable there from a synchronous throw at this boundary -- both simply become the raw err payload, decoded/validated exactly like any other JS value of type E, and both trap identically (same diagnostic wording) if that decode fails (wrong JS kind for E), not just for a mismatched throw. When E is void (result<T> shorthand), the rejection reason's shape is never even inspected -- any reason at all becomes a bare Err(). A deadlocked/never-settling Promise for a result<T,E> export still traps with the same no-progress diagnostic as a non-result export in the same situation; no-progress/deadlock is never reinterpreted as Err regardless of result_is_wit_result, since it is a StarlingMonkey/Wasmtime-host dispatch failure with no ComponentizeJS equivalent to defer to. resolve_promise_like was updated to accept a result_is_wit_result flag and an out-parameter: on a settled rejection when result_is_wit_result is true, it now hands the rejection reason back to the caller (starling_js_dispatch_native) to decode as the Err(E) payload via the exact same decode_from_js + js_dispatch.zig decodeNative(E, ...) path a synchronous throw already uses (status 2), rather than dumping+trapping; every other branch (non-result rejection, NoProgress/deadlock, AlreadyRunning/JSException from the pump itself) is unchanged and still traps unconditionally. The JSON dispatch path (starling_js_dispatch) is unaffected: a top-level result<T,E> (a union type) always routes through native dispatch (js_dispatch.zig's typeNeedsNative), never JSON.
known_deviations.evidence: runtime/js_dispatch.cpp (resolve_promise_like, starling_js_dispatch_native), runtime/js_dispatch.h (starling_js_dispatch_native doc comment); tests/compat/fixtures/promises-result (fulfillment + matching-shape rejection, including E-is-void), tests/compat/fixtures/promises-result-rejected-wrong-shape (mismatched-shape rejection traps), tests/compat/fixtures/promises-result-deadlock (deadlock still traps for a result export) -- all reference-verified via tests/compat/reference/run-reference.mjs against the pinned ComponentizeJS 0.21.0 release and build-verified via tests/compat/runtime/run-bridge-tests.sh (real Wasmtime 42 crate invoker), 2026-07-14. Also cross-checked directly (isolated single-call-per-instance experiments, since a trapped Wasmtime component instance is poisoned for further calls in the same store): ordinary fulfillment; synchronous throw matching/not-matching E's shape; Promise.reject with a raw string/number/plain value matching E's shape; Promise.reject with an Error object or plain object not matching a string E (both traps, same diagnostic wording as the equivalent synchronous-throw mismatch); E-is-void rejection of arbitrary shape; and a never-settling Promise for both void-E and payload-E result exports (traps with the same 'event loop error, but no exception is pending' diagnostic as the non-result promises-deadlock fixture).

known_deviations.summary: sync-value-parity and wit-imports were developed independently from the same base (bb97251) and each added exactly one new StarlingJsTag/NativeTag member, both numbered 9: sync-value-parity's STARLING_JS_BYTES/.bytes (list<u8>, a genuine Uint8Array) and wit-imports' STARLING_JS_UNDEFINED/.undefined_ (a void import result, JS `undefined`). Integrating both branches required renumbering exactly one of the two to avoid a silent collision; STARLING_JS_BYTES/.bytes kept its original value 9 (the older, already-fixture-verified tag) and STARLING_JS_UNDEFINED/.undefined_ was reassigned to 10 in both runtime/js_dispatch.h (C++/WABT-facing) and runtime/js_dispatch.zig (NativeTag), which must always carry identical numeric values for every tag -- verified consistent across both files (no other file hardcodes a tag's numeric value; WABT-generated code calls js_dispatch.encodeNative/decodeNative symbolically and never spells out a tag number). STARLING_JS_OPTION_NONE (5) is unaffected and remains distinct from both.

The pinned cataggar/wabt generator and ComponentizeJS 0.21.0 both support flags through 32 labels and reject flags with more than 32 labels. StarlingMonkey's generator rejection is deterministic and names the type/interface/label count; the reference fails component construction with 'cannot have more than 32 flags'. Multiword flags are therefore a shared limitation rather than a 0.21 compatibility gap. Resources and root-level imports remain separate StarlingMonkey gaps; canonical async functions, futures, and streams are also rejected by the pinned reference and are follow-on features rather than 0.21 release requirements.

known_deviations.evidence: tests/compat/reference/contracts/run.mjs and expected-0.21.0.json verify ComponentizeJS 0.21.0 at 32/33/64/65 labels. The pinned cataggar/wabt commit 491d5725f6692fdb284b920a6ddfc1a4b854580b enforces the same `labels.len <= 32` boundary in component_bindgen.zig; tests/e2e/wit-imports runtime-verifies the supported representation with a three-label flags type but does not itself exercise the 32-label boundary.

Includes a record nested inside another record.

Covers both nested result<T,E> (record field, {tag,val} JS shape) and an export's own top-level result<T,E> return type (Ok returns directly, Err signaled by throw). A Promise settling on a top-level result<T,E> export is treated the same as a synchronous return/throw (fulfillment is Ok, a rejection whose reason's JS shape matches E is Err); see known_deviations promise-result-rejection-matches-throw.

Multi-word kebab-case WIT identifiers: record fields/flags labels camelCased at the JS boundary, enum/variant case labels keep kebab-case string spelling, and function export names resolved via a camelCase fallback (see bridge known_deviations none needed -- this matches ComponentizeJS's own convention exactly, not a deviation).

Reverse direction (JavaScript imports a host-provided WIT interface function) via WABT `--js-imports`-generated canonical-ABI wrappers (runtime/js_dispatch.{h,cpp,zig}'s wit_imports::install/starling_js_import_dispatch), sharing the same encode_to_js/decode_from_js and STARLING_JS_* tag vocabulary as the export bridge above with the encode/decode roles reversed -- bool/integers/f32/f64/char/string/list<u8>/list/option/record/tuple/enum/flags/variant/result and a void result (JS `undefined`, never `false`/`null`) are all bridgeable. Not part of this compat harness (which only drives the export direction); see the dedicated tests/e2e/wit-imports/ fixture and its `zig build wit-imports-e2e-test` suite, run separately from compat-test/compat-bridge-test. Resource-typed imports, async imports, and root-level (non-interface) function imports are rejected at build time by the WABT bindgen fork rather than silently omitted; see README.md's 'WIT interface imports' section.

A returned Promise/thenable is pumped to completion via EventLoop::pump_until_promise_settled, then its fulfilled value is lowered exactly like a directly-returned value. For a non-result export, rejection and no-progress (deadlock) both surface as deterministic call-time traps rather than hanging; see known_deviations promise-exports-pumped. For a top-level WIT result<T,E> export, a settled rejection is instead treated exactly like a synchronous throw (Err(reason) if reason's JS shape matches E, trap otherwise); no-progress/deadlock is never reinterpreted as Err regardless -- see known_deviations promise-result-rejection-matches-throw.

cases.notes: Top-level export return type is the export's own result<T,E>: success returns the Ok payload directly from JS (no {tag,val} wrapper at the JS boundary), and the canonical-ABI value observed through Wasmtime is Val::Result(Ok(5)).
Failure is signaled by the JS export throwing; both the pinned ComponentizeJS reference and the current bridge translate any thrown value into Val::Result(Err(..)).
result<s32> (E is void, WIT's err-omitted shorthand): the invoker's Val::Result(Err(None)) round-trips to bare {"tag":"err"} with no "val" key.

Component-model-level record field names are the literal WIT identifiers (kebab-case, e.g. "first-value"); camelCasing (firstValue) is purely a JS-object-property detail internal to each pipeline's own JS boundary, not observable at the Wasmtime Val::Record level this invoker inspects.

fixtures.description: A Promise export that never settles at all (no rejection, no fulfillment, nothing ever queued to advance it). Must surface as a deterministic call-time trap rather than hang the host. Kept as its own single-case fixture for the same reason as 'promises-rejected' (a trapped component instance is poisoned for any further call in the same store).

expect_error.bridge_message_contains: returned a Promise that never settled
expect_error.bridge_source: runtime/event_loop.cpp: EventLoop::pump_until_promise_settled returns PromisePumpResult::NoProgress once both the microtask queue (js::RunJobs) and the async task queue (api::AsyncTask::select) are exhausted while the promise is still Pending; js_dispatch.cpp's resolve_promise_like prints a deterministic diagnostic to stderr ("...returned a Promise that never settled -- the JavaScript job queue and async task queue both ran empty while it was still pending (deadlock)") and returns false so the dispatch entry point traps (bare wasm 'unreachable'), rather than looping forever. This is the deterministic no-progress/deadlock diagnostic required by the promise-sync roadmap phase, not a hang. build-verified via tests/compat/runtime/run-bridge-tests.sh (real Wasmtime 42 crate invoker, which captured this exact diagnostic text on the guest's WASI stderr pipe, 2026-07-14); also cross-checked via tests/e2e/native-dispatch/run.sh's 'promise-deadlock' case, which wraps every wasmtime CLI invocation in a 30s timeout as an independent safety net and observed a fast trap, well under the timeout. The pinned ComponentizeJS 0.21.0 reference (reference_message_contains above) independently detects the same condition -- its own embedded engine's event-loop driver aborts with 'Error while (call) event loop error, but no exception is pending. Aborting, since that doesn't seem recoverable at all.' rather than hanging -- reference-verified via tests/compat/reference/run-reference.mjs, 2026-07-14: componentize() succeeds, and the componentized output traps deterministically (well under a manual 20s timeout probe) when invoked through the same tests/compat/runtime/invoker used for the bridge. The exact diagnostic wording differs between the two independent implementations (expected -- see bridge_message_contains), but both surface a deterministic call-time trap rather than a hang, matching this fixture's requirement.

fixtures.description: Integration fixture (feat/js-bridge-parity-integration): async (Promise-returning) counterparts to advanced-types' 'divide'/'checked-negate', confirming a Promise settling on a top-level WIT result<T, E> export is treated identically to a synchronous return/throw at this same boundary: fulfillment lowers as Ok, and rejection with a reason whose JS shape matches E also lowers as Err(reason) -- not a hard dispatch failure -- exactly like a synchronous throw of that same value would; when E is void, any rejection reason at all (any shape) becomes a bare Err(). See known_deviations 'promise-result-rejection-matches-throw' for the full empirical evidence. Only the never-trapping sub-cases are combined here (a trapped Wasmtime component instance is poisoned for further calls in the same store); the two trapping sub-cases -- a mismatched-shape rejection, and a never-settling Promise -- are each their own single-case fixture ('promises-result-rejected-wrong-shape', 'promises-result-deadlock'), for the same reason as 'promises-rejected'/'promises-deadlock'.

cases.notes: Async fulfillment of a top-level result<T,E> export lowers as Ok(value), exactly like advanced-types' synchronous 'divide-ok'.

Promise rejection with a reason whose JS shape matches E (a raw string) lowers as Err(reason), just like advanced-types' synchronous-throw 'divide-err' case -- the empirical basis for this integration's Promise-vs-result reconciliation (see known_deviations 'promise-result-rejection-matches-throw').

result<s32> (E is void): the rejection reason's shape is never inspected, so a plain-object rejection still becomes a bare Err() with no 'val' key, same as advanced-types' synchronous 'checked-negate-err' case.

fixtures.description: Integration fixture (feat/js-bridge-parity-integration): a Promise rejection on a top-level result<u32, string> export whose reason is an Error object, not a raw string -- the wrong JS shape for E. Must trap, exactly like a synchronous throw of that same Error object would (advanced-types' 'divide' never itself exercises the mismatched-shape sub-case): 'wrong-kind value traps, no coercion' applies equally whether the err payload arrives via a synchronous throw or an async rejection. Kept as its own single-case fixture for the same reason as 'promises-rejected'/'promises-deadlock'. See known_deviations 'promise-result-rejection-matches-throw'.

expect_error.bridge_source: runtime/js_dispatch.cpp: resolve_promise_like's Rejected branch, when result_is_wit_result is true, hands the rejection reason (the Error object) to starling_js_dispatch_native's existing decode_from_js (which decodes any JS object, including an Error, as a generic STARLING_JS_RECORD) + js_dispatch.zig's decodeNative(string, ...) path -- the same one a synchronous throw already goes through -- which panics with 'native dispatch: expected a string result, got a JavaScript value of kind record' since a record was decoded where E=string was expected; build-verified via tests/compat/runtime/run-bridge-tests.sh promises-result-rejected-wrong-shape, 2026-07-14.

cases.notes: Exercises the s64 upper boundary (i64::MAX) with a full-domain (> Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) value on both sides. Deliberately avoids any negative s64 value: see known_deviations componentizejs-s64-negative-value-defect -- the pinned ComponentizeJS 0.21.0 reference traps unconditionally on *any* negative s64 argument or return value, so a near-i64::MIN case cannot be expressed as a normal passing fixture case here (a trap also poisons the shared Wasmtime component instance for every later call in the same invocation, so it can't safely coexist with this fixture's other cases either); the current Zig/WABT native bridge itself is unaffected (build-verified: tests/e2e/native-dispatch/run.sh 'big-sub near i64::MIN' case).
Both JavaScript null and undefined lower back to WIT none.
Deliberately wraps past u64::MAX (mod 2**64) to also exercise BigInt wraparound arithmetic identically in both pipelines, not just round-tripping.
